questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests knowledge of bit tricks and boundary handling for 32-bit values. Rotations require combining shifted parts without branching.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise rotation using shifts
- Modulo behavior for bit widths
- Signed vs unsigned handling in C/JS contexts

## Code Example
```javascript
function rotl32(n, k) {
  k = k & 31; // 0..31
  return ((n << k) | (n >>> (32 - k))) >>> 0;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you implement rotl64 in C for uint64_t, ensuring performance on common compilers?
- Could you map this to intrinsic functions (e.g., __builtin_rotate) on supported platforms?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests branchless bitwise selection across a 128-bit value. It mirrors practical use cases like compositing two 128-bit values with a mask in a single pass.

## Key Concepts

- Branchless bitwise selection
- 128-bit composition via hi/lo fields
- Handling of full-range masks across both lanes

## Code Example

```c
uint128 blend128(uint128 a, uint128 b, uint128 mask) {
  uint128 t1 = and128(a, mask);
  uint128 t2 = and128(b, not128(mask));
  return or128(t1, t2);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you validate correctness across all 2^128 mask patterns efficiently?
- How would this approach extend to 256-bit operands with the same interface?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to apply fixed-width bit twiddling to real data without loops, a common pattern in systems programming.

## Key Concepts
- Byte masking with constants like 0x00FF00FF
- Cross-byte shifts (8 bits)
- Predictable, branch-free manipulation

## Code Example
```javascript
uint32_t swapAdjacentBytes32(uint32_t x) {
  return ((x & 0x00FF00FF) << 8) | ((x & 0xFF00FF00) >> 8);
}
```
